source.title_on_document: AIdeation: Designing a Human-AI Collaborative Ideation System for Concept Designers

supplement.where: Appendices A-F in this PDF, pp. 24-28; Appendix A is referenced on p. 12, Sec. 6.1.4.
supplement.holds: Summative questionnaire (A), summative interview questions (B), and prompts/examples for Idea Generation GPT (C), Keyword Extraction GPT (D), Combining Idea GPT (E), and Modify By Instruction GPT (F). No additional outcome estimates or standard errors are reported in these appendices.

paper_design_summary: Three main studies involved 22 distinct professional environment concept designers: formative interviews with 12, a summative within-person comparison with 16, and a one-week field deployment with 8 summative participants in 4 studios (p. 6, Sec. 4.1; p. 13, Sec. 6.1.6; p. 16, Sec. 8.1). The summative study compared AIdeation with each designer's preferred workflow, which could include generative AI, using 30-minute tasks in counterbalanced conditions and 7-point self-reported preference ratings; randomization was not stated and no external expert evaluation of outputs was conducted (pp. 12-13, Secs. 6-6.1.5). The formative interviews and field diaries/interviews supplied qualitative feedback; field tables also report descriptive idea-use and project-time statistics, without a randomized or quantitatively scored creativity/diversity contrast (p. 6, Secs. 4.2-4.3; pp. 16-17, Sec. 8 and Tables 2-3; p. 20, Sec. 9.4.1).

assignment.what_was_assigned: No AI intervention or comparison conditions were assigned. Participants described their existing design workflows, past projects, and current AI tool use in interviews; transcripts underwent thematic analysis.
assignment.quote: Each participant took part in a 1-2 hour interview covering three main topics:

participants.who: Professional environment concept designers from animation, games, art outsourcing, and freelancing. Six also participated in the summative study (S1); these are overlapping samples.
participants.quote: In the formative study, we worked with 12 environment concept designers (P1-P12)

ai_tool.name_model: No assigned tool; interviews covered existing AI tool use.
ai_tool.how_used: Participants described their prior uses of AI in research, brainstorming, and image generation. This was a needs-finding interview study, not an AI-assistance experiment (pp. 6-8, Secs. 4.2-4.3).

task.description: Interviews about typical concept-design workflows, past projects, research and brainstorming, references, and current AI use. Thematic analysis identified workflow challenges and system requirements; no creativity or diversity scores on participant outputs were reported (p. 6, Secs. 4.2-4.3).

studies.label: Field study (uncontrolled deployment in commercial projects)

assignment.what_was_assigned: All participating studios received AIdeation for use in current projects alongside their other tools. There was no randomized allocation or concurrent comparison group; original-workflow times were participant estimates, not times observed in a control condition.
assignment.quote: We asked designers to incorporate AIdeation into their current projects, emphasizing its use during early ideation alongside other design tools.

arms.name: AIdeation in ongoing commercial projects
arms.description: Uncontrolled deployment alongside each studio's other design tools, with diaries and follow-up interviews (p. 16, Sec. 8.2).

participants.who: Eight professional environment concept designers in four studios, all recruited from the summative study (S1). Studios worked in visual effects for animation, films and television, art outsourcing, and games. Studio counts and generated-idea counts are not additional people.
participants.quote: We recruited 8 participants across 4 studios (S1-S4) from the summative study

ai_tool.name_model: AIdeation (Idea Generation GPT on gpt-4o-2024-05-13, GPT-4o Vision captioning, DALL-E 3 images, Bing Image Search API)
ai_tool.how_used: The same AIdeation system as in the summative study was deployed separately for each studio. Designers used it during early ideation in ongoing commercial projects alongside their other tools (p. 11, Sec. 5.2.1; p. 16, Sec. 8.2).

task.description: Commercial environment design, matte painting, and visual development. Diaries and interviews documented workflows, selected ideas, self-assessed creativity and quality, and participant reports of director/client feedback. Tables 2-3 report descriptive AI-generated/selected idea counts and actual project time versus estimated time for the original workflow; no quantitative creativity/diversity scoring contrast was reported (pp. 16-17, Secs. 8.2-8.3 and Tables 2-3; p. 20, Sec. 9.4.1).
task.duration: One-week deployment; 30-minute follow-up online interviews (p. 16, Secs. 8-8.2)

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Within this paper, six formative participants (S2) also took part in the summative study (S1), and all eight field-study participants (S3) came from S1. The paper reports 22 distinct participants across the three main studies; their study counts must not be added as independent samples. Cross-paper overlap is not stated.
sample_overlap.quote: 6 participants (P1-P6) had also participated in the earlier formative study.

company_involvement.description: The acknowledgments name support from Moonshine Studio, Winking Studios, and Rayark Games, alongside National Taiwan University. The form of company support is not specified; the acknowledgment does not establish financial sponsorship or AI-vendor involvement.

eligibility.reason: The summative study analyzes 16 people completing both conditions, below 50; condition/topic order was counterbalanced but randomization is not stated (pp. 12-13, Secs. 6.1.1 and 6.1.6). Its creativity and idea-quality outcomes are self-reported preferences, and no external expert evaluation of outputs was conducted (p. 13, Sec. 6.1.5; p. 24, Appendix A). The formative study comprises interviews with 12 designers, without an assigned AI intervention or scored-output contrast (p. 6, Secs. 4.1-4.3). The uncontrolled field deployment includes 8 of the summative participants in 4 studios for one week; creativity/quality feedback is qualitative, and its idea-use counts and actual-versus-estimated workflow times do not supply a scored creativity/diversity comparison (pp. 16-17, Secs. 8-8.3 and Tables 2-3; p. 20, Sec. 9.4.1). The paper reports only 22 distinct participants across the three main studies (p. 6, Sec. 4.1; p. 7, Table 1). No study qualifies for the core or the defined context classes.

one_line_finding: In a within-subject comparison, 16 professional concept designers rated AIdeation over their own workflow for enhancing creativity (mean 5.56 on a 7-point preference scale, p = 0.001; p. 13) but not for idea quality (mean 4.31, p = 0.41; p. 14); all measures are self-reported.
notes: S1 retains the original summative-study ID; S2 and S3 add the formative and field studies. Empty outcomes arrays for S2 and S3 indicate no qualifying quantitatively scored creativity/diversity outcome; their qualitative findings and descriptive usage/time reporting are described in the study entries. For the noncomparative interview study and uncontrolled deployment, assignment.structure is left empty because the form provides no noncomparative category. The task-design pilot described within the summative methods involved two professional designers who could not complete the initial 40-minute task; it informed removal of sketching and reports no scored creativity/diversity outcome (p. 12, Sec. 6.1.3). The complete markdown, including Appendices A-F, was read; recorded numbers and correction passages were checked against the PDF.
